title: Counting Out a Number
short: Give exactly the number of objects asked for.
trouble: Children keep counting past the number asked for because they do not stop at the target.

blocks.html: Sometimes you need to give out a number of things: “Please bring me 6 spoons.” That means count and stop at 6.

blocks.name: counters
blocks.cap: Add or take away counters to make a group of exactly 6. Then count to check.

blocks.html: To count out a number, say the number first. Then count, and stop when you say it.
The last number you say tells how many you have. So when you say 6, you have 6. Taking one more would make 7.

blocks.title: Six crackers
blocks.q: Get exactly 6 crackers from a box of 15.
steps: Stop! You have 6. The rest stay in the box.

blocks.html: Counting right past the number, because the counting words keep going. Say the target out loud first, and hold up that many fingers to remember it.
For grown-ups: Ask your child to bring exactly 7 napkins or 5 crayons. Count together to check.

sources.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Kindergarten, K.CC.B.5: given a number from 1 to 20, count out that many objects
